title: Senate Floor Debate
subtitle: S.1842 — Climate Resilience and Clean Energy Investment Act

metadata.laymanSummary: A sweeping climate and clean energy bill failed in the Senate, with its $450 billion price tag and renewable energy mandates driving opposition from moderates on both sides.

data.billTitle: Climate Resilience and Clean Energy Investment Act — $450B for renewable energy, grid modernization, and climate adaptation

speakers.name: Sen. Sheldon Whitehouse
speakers.title: D-RI · Senate Environment Chair
speakers.quote: The 12 hottest years in recorded history have all been in the last 15 years. Insurance companies are exiting states. Wildfires now burn year-round. Hurricanes are category 4 before they would have been category 2. We can pay now — or we can pay catastrophically later. This bill is the cheapest climate insurance policy ever written.

speakers.name: Sen. Bernie Sanders
speakers.title: I-VT · Senate HELP
speakers.quote: Let me be clear: the fossil fuel industry has known about the consequences of carbon emissions since the 1970s and they hid it. They paid politicians to deny it. They are still paying. The difference between a $450 billion climate investment and doing nothing is the difference between a livable planet and economic collapse.

speakers.name: Sen. Ted Cruz
speakers.title: R-TX · Senate Commerce
speakers.quote: Texas produces more wind energy than any state in the nation — and we did it without 450 billion dollars in government subsidies. Real energy policy trusts markets, not bureaucrats picking winners. This bill would destroy affordable energy in pursuit of an environmental ideology that has failed everywhere it has been tried.

data.title: What This Vote Means
data.text: S.1842 failed 48-51, blocked by three Democratic moderates from fossil fuel states joining all Republicans. The bill would have invested $450 billion in solar, wind, and grid modernization, established a clean electricity standard requiring 80% carbon-free power by 2035, and funded climate adaptation for coastal communities. The defeat leaves US climate policy in limbo ahead of an international summit.
